NextItNet uses residual causal dilated convolutions to expand historical coverage without pooling; its receptive field is structurally determined, rather than selected by input content. The search found related gating research, but no verified 2023–2026 NextItNet extension matching the proposed mechanism. [Original NextItNet paper](https://fajieyuan.github.io/papers/nextitnet6.pdf). Relevant adjacent work: [GAT4Rec (2024)](https://www.mdpi.com/2227-7390/12/14/2189) uses a GRU-derived signal to gate input representations before Transformer processing; [MLM4Rec (2024)](https://doi.org/10.1145/3638562) combines convolutional gated MLPs with multiple local granularities. These support content-dependent filtering as a design direction, without establishing benefits for NextItNet.

[Dilated Convolution with Learnable Spacings (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.06383) learns kernel spacings through differentiable interpolation, offering another route to receptive-field adaptation. Its evidence concerns vision, audio and speech; learned spacings do not by themselves establish per-input temporal selection or recommendation gains.

Practical hypothesis, inferred from these sources: retain NextItNet’s residual causal backbone and single scoring head, but apply jointly trained sigmoid gates to historical contributions entering each dilated convolution. Condition gates only on information available at that output position; preserve padding masks and final-nonpadding readout. Compare against the corrected baseline under the fixed validation protocol. Diagnose complete-output prefix sensitivity by replacing or removing older prefixes while preserving the recent suffix and its positions, then recomputing scores through the entire network. Measure score changes, top-10 overlap and validation HR@10 changes across suffix lengths. Existing diagnostics do not establish excessive dependence on older interactions; reduced sensitivity alone would not establish improvement.
